short: Effect of Ca addition on grain refinement of Mg-9Li-1Al allo
title: Effect of Ca addition on grain refinement of Mg-9Li-1Al alloy

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Duplex Mg-Li alloys solidify with very coarse lamellar alpha-Mg and coarse beta-Li grains, which limits their usable properties. A small Ca addition should form Al2Ca particles that nucleate both alpha-Mg and beta-Li heterogeneously and refine the structure.
states.detail: Absorbed: g1 (HYP/need), g2 (HYP/hypothesis), g3 (DES/base_system), g4 (DES/modification), g5 (DES/variable_sweep), g6 (PRC/forming), g7 (PRC/treatment). Premises: Mg-40Sr and Mg-30Y master alloys refine the beta-Li phase of Mg-14Li

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Al2Ca forms in the Ca-bearing alloy alongside alpha-Mg and beta-Li and is absent from LA91. Sub-micron to ~1 um Al2Ca particles lie along the alpha/beta phase boundaries and inside both matrices, before and after extrusion.
states.detail: Absorbed: g8 (STR/phase/identity), g9 (STR/microstructure/distribution), g10 (STR/microstructure/shape), g11 (STR/microstructure/feature_size), g13 (STR/interface). Premises: From the Mg-Al ternary diagram the solubility of Al in Mg on solidification exceeds the 1 wt% Al of LA91; Edge-to-edge matching model: a nucleant is potent when matching close-packed planes differ by under 6% and matching directions by under 10%; beta-Li is bcc with a = 0.351 nm and Al2Ca has a = 0.804 nm, with three near close-packed planes each

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Non-deforming Al2Ca particles act as heterogeneous nuclei for alpha-Mg on solidification and as dynamic-recrystallisation nucleation sites for beta-Li during extrusion. The refined duplex structure is expected to raise yield strength through the Hall-Petch relation
states.detail: Absorbed: g12 (MEC/pathway), g14 (PRP/value). Premises: Edge-to-edge matching model: a nucleant is potent when matching close-packed planes differ by under 6% and matching directions by under 10%; Hall-Petch: a smaller grain size raises yield strength by adding boundary area that impedes dislocation motion

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: 0.2 wt% Ca forms crystallographically potent Al2Ca that refines both alpha-Mg and beta-Li in Mg-9Li-1Al, cast and extruded

nodes.title: SEM:BSE, F2, F4
nodes.head: Backscatter contrast puts bright particles in strings along curvilinear phase boundaries and as isolated specks inside the matrix of the as-cast Ca alloy. In the extruded Ca alloy bright particles are spread over the whole field, with one ~3 um agglomerate in the marked region and sub-micron particles on the boundaries
nodes.solves: Sub-micron to ~1 um Al2Ca particles lie along the alpha/beta phase boundaries and inside both matrices, before and after extrusion

nodes.title: OPTICAL, F1, F3
nodes.head: Against the 100 um bars the Ca-free lamellae run past 300 um and leave the frame, while the Ca-bearing blocks measure roughly 20-50 um. After identical extrusion the beta grains measure about 10 um without Ca and 4-5 um with Ca at the same 25 um scale bar
nodes.solves: Ca refines both phases: as-cast alpha-Mg to ~28 um and as-extruded beta-Li from 10.32 to 4.56 um

nodes.title: TEM:SAED, F6
nodes.head: The simulated overlay of Li-matrix and Al2Ca spot patterns shows three parallel delta-g vectors, 311A/110L, 715A/222L and 404A/112L, about one habit-plane trace. Of the close-packed plane pairs only {311}Al2Ca/{110}beta-Li has an interplanar misfit below the 6% critical value
nodes.solves: Al2Ca and beta-Li share the only plane pair below the 6% critical misfit, {311}Al2Ca/{110}beta-Li, with parallel close-packed directions
nodes.note: only this one zone-axis pair is drawn; the other orientation relationships are said to follow in the same way but are not shown
